decisions.decision: The bounded-window binary semi-Markovian world is encoded PURELY ALGEBRAICALLY over Mathlib plus `Causalean.Graph.DAG`, not over `Causalean.SCM.Model.SCM` / `SWIGGraph`. Vertices are `Win Vlab H := Vlab x Fin (H+1)` (index `i` denotes time `i - H`); a summary graph is `structure SummaryGraph Vlab where dir : Finset (Vlab x Vlab); bi : Finset (Sym2 Vlab)`; a refinement is `structure Refinement Vlab H where dir : Finset (Win x Win); bi : Finset (Sym2 Win); bi_offDiag`. A model is `structure BinaryModel G` carrying a padded latent-support size, per-factor weight vectors on `Fin C`, deterministic Boolean tables, and the two locality fields (a table at `v` depends only on `G`-parent coordinates and on factors incident to `v`); the latent index type is `inductive FactorIdx | priv (v : Win) | edge (e : Sym2 Win)`.
decisions.why: The note's content is (i) a FINITE ENUMERATION of refinements as data with a cardinality bound, (ii) MULTI-AFFINITY of `P_G` and `q_G` in independent latent-factor weight vectors, (iii) COMPACTNESS of a finite disjoint union of products of simplices, and (iv) exact rational arithmetic on explicit 16- and 8-dimensional vectors. `Causalean.SCM.Model.SCM` is a kernel-valued, `SWIGGraph`-indexed dependent structure whose graph field carries twelve proof obligations and whose bidirected edges are DERIVED (`SWIGGraph.directlyConfounded` = share an unobserved parent) rather than given as an explicit edge set; ranging a `Finset` over 2^(m_dir + m_bi) such structures, and reading the polynomial degree of a kernel composite, are both out of reach at that abstraction. Surveyed and recorded as bypass-justified in `substrate_survey`. The DIRECTED layer is nevertheless genuinely reused: `Causalean.DAG` is exactly a decidable edge relation on a `Fintype` with cycle-freeness, and `DAG.acyclic_of_topoOrder` (with the time coordinate as the numbering) discharges acyclicity of every positive-lag refinement and of the supergraph `D_{H,L}(S)` in one line, while `DAG.ancestralSet` IS the reflexive directed ancestral closure `An_D(.)`.

decisions.decision: `ass:structural-recursion` is the fixed-point Prop `StructuralRecursion G M ev := forall u v, ev u v = M.table v (ev u) u`, with the SIGNATURE restriction of `f_v` (dependence only on `pa_G(v)` and on factors `a` incident to `v`) carried as two non-member fields `parentLocal` / `incidenceLocal` of the `BinaryModel` carrier. F2 additionally builds `BinaryModel.eval` by recursion on the time coordinate and proves `StructuralRecursion G M M.eval` from positive lags plus `parentLocal`; the interventional recursion is `BinaryModel.interv` (the same recursion with a `Finset Win` of coordinates overridden).
decisions.why: The frozen condition is an equation, so the assumption atom must be a Prop, and a dependent-subtype table `{0,1}^(pa_G v) -> ... -> Bool` would make the whole compiler dependent on `G` through its parent Finsets and block the `Fintype` instance needed to enumerate the branch catalogue. Keeping the two locality clauses on the carrier follows the same pattern as the accepted `scm_propensity_lv_sharpness_frontier` plan (its F1-D9): the canonical declaration still unfolds to the full frozen construction, and no defining clause is dropped.

decisions.decision: `ass:independent-edge-latents` is the FACTORIZATION Prop `IndependentEdgeLatents M mu := forall u, mu u = prod over a of M.weight a (u a)`, asserted of the joint latent mass `mu : LatentAssign M -> Real` that the compatibility and query definitions integrate against.
decisions.why: Mutual independence of a finite family of finitely supported variables is exactly factorization of the joint mass into the marginals; on a finite index set this is the statement the proofs actually use (the disjoint-block independence steps of lem:positive-lag-cyclic-cde-adjustment (8), lem:tiv-summary-iv-representation (3), and the parity-tilt determinant (30) are all instances). Using `ProbabilityTheory.iIndepFun` would force a measure-theoretic ambient space that nothing else in the plan needs.

decisions.decision: `def:sharp-envelope`, `def:order-only-envelope`, `def:confidence-endpoints` and `def:contrast-confidence-interval` are thin instantiations of `Causalean.PartialID.IdentifiedInterval obj feasible = Set.range (fun x : {x // feasible x} => obj x)`: `attainableCDESet` is the identified interval of `microCDE` over `summaryFiber`, and each endpoint pair is `sInf` / `sSup` of it. The two confidence nodes take the empty-fiber case literally: `if Q = emptyset then emptyset else Set.Icc (sInf Q) (sSup Q)`.
decisions.why: `IdentifiedInterval` is the exact right abstraction (the attained value set of an objective over a feasible set) and brings `mem_identifiedInterval` and `identifiedInterval_subset_Icc` for free; those are the two moves that thm:sharp-refinement-envelope (5)-(8), lem:refinement-embeds-complete-order and thm:simultaneous-whole-set-inference make. Verified by reading `Causalean/PO/ID/Partial/Basic.lean:22-116` (namespace `Causalean.PartialID`). `identifiedInterval_eq_Icc` (read at `Basic.lean:78-84`) is DELIBERATELY NOT part of any node's reuse support or proof route: it requires `hconn : (IdentifiedInterval obj feasible).OrdConnected`, and this note's honest scope explicitly disclaims connectedness ('the envelope is the smallest closed interval containing all attainable CDE values; the attainable set itself need not be connected'), so that premise is unavailable and no node may assert that its attained value set equals a `Set.Icc`. Every endpoint claim is therefore stated and proved as a SEPARATELY DEFINED attained infimum/supremum of the value set (`envelopeLower := sInf`, `envelopeUpper := sSup`), discharged from compactness of the feasible set plus `IsLeast.csInf_eq` / `IsGreatest.csSup_eq`. The nodes remain `define-local` because each is a specific instantiation with fixed arguments, not the generic declaration; the generic declaration is recorded in `reuse_support`.

decisions.decision: The two `status: cited` lemmas (`lem:one-block-real-algebraic-elimination`, `lem:multiblock-real-algebraic-qe`) are frozen `carrier: logical-claim` substrate gates: named `Sort 0` propositions, `gate: true`, `gate_class: cited`, `defer_tier: true`, excluded from `theorems`, listed in `infrastructure_needed[]`, and THREADED as explicit hypotheses `(hElim1 : OneBlockRealAlgebraicElimination)` into `thm:exact-algebraic-certification` and `(hQE : MultiBlockRealAlgebraicQE)` into `thm:factorization-safe-quotient-obstruction` — the only two nodes whose `depends_on` names them. `def:exact-certifier` (`certify`) also takes `hElim1` as a Lean argument and extracts its procedure by `Classical.choice`.
decisions.why: Mathlib has NO semialgebraic sets, NO Tarski-Seidenberg / quantifier elimination, and NO Positivstellensatz: `lean_loogle '"Semialgebraic"'` returns nothing and `lean_loogle '"RealClosed"'` returns only the `IsRealClosed` field axioms in `Mathlib.FieldTheory.IsRealClosed.Basic` (odd-degree roots, square dichotomy), with `lean_leansearch 'quantifier elimination for real closed fields, Tarski-Seidenberg, semialgebraic sets'` returning nothing on point. Building block-structured real quantifier elimination with Basu-Pollack-Roy arithmetic-operation, degree, and coefficient-height bounds is a major upstream Mathlib contribution and is genuinely infeasible inside this artifact, so both nodes are gates even though the first is the engine of thm:exact-algebraic-certification. Their consumers stay IN SCOPE (`defer_tier: false`) and are proved CONDITIONAL on them.

decisions.decision: The gate `OneBlockRealAlgebraicElimination` carries ONLY what the source states: an elimination procedure deciding feasibility and returning a one-free-variable projection, with an ARITHMETIC-OPERATION count `B^(O(1)) (s_G D_G)^(O(k_G))`, output univariate degree `D_G^(O(k_G))`, output coefficient bit length `B (s_G D_G)^(O(k_G))`, and exact real-algebraic sample points in nonempty sign cells. The BIT-OPERATION bound in `thm:exact-algebraic-certification` is NOT in the gate: it is derived inside that theorem from the arithmetic count together with the coefficient-bit-length control, and the aggregation over the `R_Sigma` branches is likewise theorem content. All `O(.)` constants are encoded as existentially quantified naturals (`exists c, cost <= R_Sigma * B^c * (s_max * D_max)^(c * k_max)`).
decisions.why: The frozen `attestation` on lem:one-block-real-algebraic-elimination says verbatim: 'The source states arithmetic-operation complexity plus bit-size growth; any claimed bit-operation form is a derived corollary and must be reviewed as such, not attributed verbatim.' Putting the bit-operation bound into the citation would misattribute it; putting the branch aggregation into the citation would launder paper-owned content.

In particular the complexity clause of thm:exact-algebraic-certification is stated about a cost functional SUPPLIED BY the gate (so its content is the R_Sigma aggregation and the derivation of `R_Sigma, k_max, s_max, D_max` from `d, H, L, E_S^{dir}, E_S^{bi}` and the branch catalogues), not as a model-independent inequality; and the 'Cert terminates' clause is stated as totality of the Lean function `certify` together with the two-branch output-validity predicate, not as a vacuous claim.

env.world: A finite nonempty label set \(\mathcal V\) of \(d=|\mathcal V|\) binary component processes is observed on the bounded past window \(\mathbb T_H=\{-H,\ldots,0\}\), giving the \(N=d(H+1)\) observed vertices \(\mathcal W_H=\mathcal V\times\mathbb T_H\). Causal knowledge is a lag-abstracted summary causal graph \(\mathcal S=(\mathcal V,E_{\mathcal S}^{\to},E_{\mathcal S}^{\leftrightarrow})\) whose directed part may contain cycles. A full-time refinement \(G=(\mathcal W_H,E_G^{\to},E_G^{\leftrightarrow})\) is an acyclic directed mixed graph on the window; the projection \(\operatorname{proj}_H\) forgets time indices while retaining edge type, \(\mathcal B_H(\mathcal S)\) collects every summary-compatible bidirected placement with distinct endpoints inside the window, and \(\mathfrak G_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) is the class of refinements whose directed lags all lie in \(\{1,\ldots,L\}\) and whose projection is exactly \(\mathcal S\); no \(L\)-bound is placed on bidirected time separations. The temporal partial order \(\preceq_H\) compares time coordinates, \(\operatorname{Pred}_H(v)\) is the set of strictly earlier vertices, and \(G_H^{\mathrm{ord}}\) is the single maximal graph carrying every strictly-earlier arrow and every bidirected pair of distinct vertices. The focal query fixes labels \(X,Y\), a lag \(\gamma\in\{1,\ldots,L\}\), the treatment vertex \(X_{-\gamma}=(X,-\gamma)\), the terminal outcome \(Y_0=(Y,0)\), the positive-lag possible-parent set \(W=\operatorname{PP}_{\mathcal S,L}(Y_0)\), the controlled set \(Z=W\setminus\{X_{-\gamma}\}\) and its assignment \(z\). The bounded positive-lag supergraph \(D_{H,L}(\mathcal S)\) carries every summary-compatible positive-lag directed placement, and \(\operatorname{An}_D(\cdot)\) is its reflexive directed ancestral closure. Distinguished instances are the three-process temporal-instrument summary graph \(\mathcal S_{\mathrm{TIV}}\) on \(\{A,X,Y\}\) with its vertex \(A_{-1}\), and the six-vertex overlapping-edge-latent kill-test graph \(G_{\mathrm{ABC}}\).

lem:finite-factor-support-reduction.statement: With `C := 2^N + card J`: every finite binary semi-Markovian model on `G` admits another model with the SAME vector \((P,(q_j)_{j\in\mathcal J})\), the same deterministic recursion, mutually independent private and pairwise exogenous parents, and every factor support of size at most `C`; after zero-padding to `Fin C` the systems range over the finite catalogue `BranchCat G`, on each branch the map from the independent factor weights to \((P,(q_j)_j)\) is multi-affine; and conversely every point of every product-of-simplices branch reconstructs a finite semi-Markovian model on `G` with the same image.
lem:finite-factor-support-reduction.notes: Search trace: `lean_leansearch 'reduce the support of a finite mixture preserving finitely many moments Caratheodory'` and `lean_leansearch 'the standard simplex is compact'` -> `isCompact_stdSimplex`, `Set.Finite.isCompact_convexHull` (`Mathlib.Analysis.Convex.Topology`), `Convex.exists_...` family, but no ready-made 'support reduction preserving a finite linear functional vector' lemma in either library; `grep 'Caratheodory|caratheodory|support reduction' ../doc/API.md` -> nothing; `Glob Causalean/PO/ID/Partial/BalkePearl/*.lean` -> `LatentTable.lean` reduces to a FIXED four-bit alphabet by construction rather than by an elimination argument, so a partial fit only. Result: build-inline. The argument is the note's own: the conditional response vectors \(b_a(u)\) lie in an affine subspace of dimension at most \(C-1\), so more than `C` positive weights give a linear dependence with zero sum, and moving to a boundary of the feasible interval kills one weight while preserving the whole image (1)-(2); this is a `Finset`-cardinality induction and is MEDIUM, not large. Its two consumers thm:sharp-refinement-envelope and thm:factorization-safe-quotient-obstruction rely on the resulting `Fintype` branch catalogue (F1-D1 (i)) and on the exact bound `C`, so F2 must keep `C` symbolic. hyps: ass:structural-recursion and ass:independent-edge-latents are named DIRECTLY because this node's `depends_on` does not list def:fixed-refinement-scm-class.

infrastructure_needed.description: One-block real quantifier elimination over the rationals with Basu-Pollack-Roy bounds: feasibility decision plus a one-free-variable projection in B^{O(1)}(s D)^{O(k)} arithmetic operations, output univariate degree D^{O(k)}, output coefficient bit length B(s D)^{O(k)}, and exact real-algebraic sample points in every nonempty sign cell.

Effective quantifier elimination for arbitrary finite first-order formulas over a real closed field with rational polynomial atoms, including alternating universal and existential variable blocks: decidability for sentences and a computable quantifier-free semialgebraic description of the solution set with free variables.
